decision.summary: target-b has ok:false with p95_s=1.665s and 5 requests, while target-a is healthy with p95_s=0.035s and 5 requests. Both workers share identical configuration (tool_call_parser=qwen2_5_coder, same chat_template, same model, same container_state=running). The high p95 latency on target-b (1.665s vs 0.035s on target-a) combined with its ok:false status indicates a performance issue on target-b. The environment description notes target-b is reached through a network proxy that can be impaired. Evidence ev-006 shows target-b route_latency_avg_s=0.204s but the per-worker probe (ev-001) shows p95_s=1.665s, suggesting the proxy or target-b's serving is degraded. The tool-call-visible probe (ev-003) confirms target-b can still process structured tool calls successfully, so the issue is latency, not functional failure.
decision.stop_reason: Evidence sufficient to identify root cause: target-b latency degradation likely due to network proxy impairment as described in the environment manifest.

repair_plan.expected_effect: Drain target-b from routing so new traffic goes only to target-a, reducing overall fleet latency.
repair_plan.risk: Low - target-b will be drained; existing in-flight requests may complete or fail, but target-a remains healthy serving traffic.
verification_plan: Re-run route-probe to confirm target-b p95_s improves or target-b is marked ok:false persists (indicating drain was successful but issue remains).
Re-run tool-call-visible on target-b to confirm structured tool calls still work after drain.
repair_plan.rollback_plan: undrain-worker action_id=undrain-worker to return target-b to rotation if needed.
